releases.title: Build Bigger, Shape Deeper, and Control More of the Engraving
releases.summary: A major workflow release adding panel-sized production, richer LightBurn exports and browser integration, operation-based Processing Palettes, and new tools for layered and geometric artwork.

groups.title: Improvements to existing workflows
items: Panel Tiling splits large Rasterizer designs across repeatable blanks and exports centered tile files, a manifest, and an assembly map.
Color Discovery can export native LightBurn Material Test presets with grids of up to 800 cells, avoiding the 30-cell limit of color-layer-based LightBurn projects.
Expanded geometry options add Halftone Newsprint, custom Glyph and Krasnow cells, tighter packing, seeded rotation, per-swatch routing, and source-image detail in Parallax SVG exports.
Job History thumbnails, steadier signed-in navigation, recoverable expired guest links, bulk swatch routing controls, and optional white engraving make everyday workflows easier to manage.

groups.title: Depthmaps and Processing Palettes
items: Depthmaps can be exported as editable LightBurn projects using Grayscale output or Galvo 3D Sliced settings with configurable passes and cleanup.
Processing Palettes organize saved LightBurn settings by material and operation, including Cut, Score, Photo, Fill, Shovel, Cleaning, and 3D-Slice roles.
Layered Relief converts depthmaps into aligned physical layers with adjustable depth groups, per-layer and full-stack previews, registration features, score guides, and optional surface engraving.

groups.title: New experimental laboratories
items: Layered Mandala Lab builds coordinated multi-sheet radial artwork with custom motifs, openwork, structural supports, and per-layer Randomize and Reset controls.

SpiralGraph Lab creates open-line or filled-ribbon drawings from resizable virtual tracks, gears, pencil reaches, and custom SVG or raster-image tracks, with independent drawing sizes and optional per-drawing palette routing.
Generated LightBurn projects remain editable starting points: inspect every layer and setting, then test on suitable scrap before running valuable work.

groups.title: LightBurn browser extension beta
items: Connect Rasterizer to local LightBurn through the Chrome/Edge browser extension beta. Requires LightBurn 2.23 or later.
Create a Color palette from selected LightBurn Material Library entries and assign each entry to a Rasterizer swatch during preview.
Import LightBurn swatches into an existing Color palette, or create a Processing palette by assigning settings to Cut, Score, Photo, Fill, Shovel, Cleaning, and 3D-Slice roles.
Imports show completion feedback; imported settings remain snapshots rather than live synchronization.
Load native .lbrn2 files up to 100 MiB from Job History, review the current project, and explicitly confirm replacement. The extension does not start the laser.
Connection, pairing, and import failure handling help recover interrupted operations. If completion is unknown, inspect LightBurn before retrying; closing a dialog does not cancel an import.
A download and installation guide covers Chrome/Edge, enabling LightBurn API access, pairing, usage, and manual updates. Extension controls appear only when the extension is enabled.
Deployment packages each download for its own website origin: Development for staging and Beta for production. Unpacked installations require manual updates.

groups.title: Deployment reliability
items: Staging deployment compares each component against its last successful deployment, so changes missed by a failed deployment remain eligible on the next run.

releases.title: Initial public checkpoint
releases.summary: The first tagged MOPA Laser Rasterizer release established the browser workflow for turning raster artwork into layered laser-ready output.

groups.title: Highlights
items: Converted raster artwork into color-separated vector geometry for laser workflows.
Generated layered SVG output and LightBurn projects backed by Material Library settings.
Introduced the core MOPA color engraving and fauxlographic experimentation workflows.

groups.title: Project foundation
items: Published the initial operator documentation and local development workflow.
Established the v1 data and output conventions that later releases continue to evolve.
